title: Grandma's phone joined my Wi-Fi 📶

hook_text: At 2:50 in the morning, a new device joined my Wi-Fi: Grandma's phone.

scenes.narration: At 2:50 in the morning, a new device joined my Wi-Fi: Grandma's phone.
Grandma passed away last spring. Her phone was buried with her. I sat up and stared at the router app.
Connected devices, five. My laptop. My phone. The TV. Grandma's phone. And one more, with no name.
I found my own number in her contacts and pressed call. Somewhere in the hallway, a phone began to ring.
A tinny, old-fashioned ring. The one she always used. It came from the end of the hall.
I stayed still. The ringing stopped. A text arrived on my phone. Grandma. Four words. You left the door.
I never leave doors open. I walked into the hall. My bedroom door was ajar. Behind me. In my own room.
The router app refreshed. The unnamed device had a name now. It was mine.
Grandma's phone buzzed once more. Do not turn around, sweetheart. It only borrows my voice when you are alone.
So tell me. Do you call it, or unplug the router?
